title: Safe opening and disassembly
summary: How to open a phone without breaking it, and how to keep track of every part.

sections.heading: Plan before you open
sections.body: Find out the construction type, and read the whole guide first. Back up your data. Let the battery run down to below 25% if you can, and power the phone off fully. Make sure you have the right replacement part before you start.

sections.heading: Using heat safely
sections.body: Heat softens adhesive, but too much damages batteries and screens. Use a heat pad or a heat gun on low. Keep the heat moving, stay on the edges, and stop when the surface is too hot to keep a finger on. It is better to warm the phone several times than to overheat it once.

sections.heading: Prying without damage
sections.body: Open a small gap with a suction cup, then slide in a plastic pick at a shallow angle. Go only a few millimeters deep, because cables and the battery can sit right at the edge. Leave picks in the seam so the glue does not close again. Never force a stuck section. Look for a screw or clip you missed.

sections.heading: Screws and connectors
sections.body: Keep screws in the order you removed them, because a long screw in a short hole can pierce the board. Disconnect the battery before anything else. Lift connectors straight up from their edges with a plastic spudger. When you put a connector back, press it straight down until it clicks.

sections.heading: Test before you close
sections.body: Before sealing the phone, connect everything and power it on. Check that the repair worked and that nothing else stopped working. Finding a problem now saves you from opening the phone twice.

quiz.question: What should you disconnect first, once the phone is open?
quiz.explanation: Disconnecting the battery first removes power from the board, so you do not cause a short.

quiz.question: How deep should an opening pick go?
options: As deep as it will go
quiz.explanation: Cables and the battery can sit close to the edge, so keep the pick shallow.

quiz.question: Why must screws be kept in order?
options: A long screw in a short hole can damage the board
quiz.explanation: Screws can differ in length, and a long one in the wrong hole can pierce the board.

quiz.question: A section of the phone will not open. What should you do?
options: Look for a screw or clip you missed
Heat it as much as you can
quiz.explanation: Force breaks parts. A stuck section often has a hidden screw or a clip you missed.
